course: DSAI4207 Introduction to Large Language Models
note: Answers are expected to be findable in data/extracted lecture text. gold_hint_source is for the team only and is NOT used at runtime.

questions.question: In the LLM lifecycle lecture slide titled "One Answer Runs on Two Clocks", what does the user see versus what makes the answer possible?
In the LLM lifecycle lecture, what do demonstrations and preferences later get called in the post-training pipeline?
What self-supervision objective does Lecture 1 describe for learning from raw text, and what loss is minimized?
What does a language model assign probabilities to, according to Lecture 2?
Write the product formula Lecture 2 gives for the probability of an entire token sequence x1:T under a language model.
At position t, how does Lecture 2 define the context x<t for next-token prediction?
Why does Lecture 2 say next-token prediction is a powerful learning signal? List the reasons it gives (free supervision, what prediction requires, unified paradigm).
In the tokenization/embeddings lecture, what is the full forward pipeline from text to next-token probability?
What fundamental trade-off does tokenization make according to the course notes, and how does BPE start?
In the tokenization and embeddings lecture, Lecture 2 defined conditional probability pθ(xt|x<t); which loss and which evaluation metric follow from that (NLL / cross-entropy → Perplexity)?
According to Lecture 4, why must tokens exchange information, and what mechanism (Q, K, V) is introduced to let them do so?
Why can a fully connected MLP not process variable-length token sequences without a mixing solution, according to Lecture 4?
In Lecture 5's Llama-2-7B parameter breakdown, roughly what share of parameters sit in the FFN versus attention, and what absolute sizes are given?
What does the residual stream store in a Transformer block according to Lecture 5, and what does a sublayer propose?
How does LayerNorm compute statistics according to Lecture 5 — across which dimension, and not across which?
According to the mixing-information / attention lecture, write the scaled dot-product self-attention formula Attention(Q, K, V), and why use multi-head attention?
According to Lecture 6, what are the three signals that can stop the generation loop?
How does Lecture 6 contrast top-k sampling with beam search?
What are the two main chapter themes of Lecture 6 (decoding vs efficient inference), and which topics fall under efficient inference?
Describe the predict → choose → append generation feedback loop from Lecture 6.
Lecture 7 frames four decisions that turn random weights into a base model. What are those four decisions?
What distributional goal does Lecture 7 state for pretraining (relating pθ and pdata)?
According to Lecture 8, why is a pretrained model not yet a useful assistant, and what does post-training change in broad terms?
Name the parameter-update methods compared in Lecture 8's Chapter II (full fine-tuning, adapters, LoRA) and one storage/cost difference mentioned for LoRA versus full fine-tuning.
Which training signals does Lecture 8 list under Chapter III (SFT, preferences, RLHF & PPO, DPO)?
In the LoRA post-training tutorial, what is the trainable update formula W′, and which matrices are trainable versus frozen?
For a 2048×2048 weight matrix with LoRA rank 8, how many trainable parameters does the tutorial example report, and what percentage of the full matrix is that?
According to Lecture 9, what stays fixed when you prompt a frozen model, and what changes compared to training?
What is chain-of-thought prompting as described in Lecture 9, and how does self-consistency use multiple reasoning paths?
In Tutorial 9's room-booking extraction lab, which four JSON output fields are required, and what are the allowed values for status?
Under Tutorial 9's time-order policy, when is status set to needs_clarification even if times are present?
According to Lecture 10, how does closed-book answering differ from answering with retrieved evidence from a reading pack?
Why can keyword/BM25-style search miss the meaning of a query according to Lecture 10?
In Lecture 10's BERTopic-style clustering discussion, what do unassigned HDBSCAN points typically become, and what does c-TF-IDF provide for a cluster?
How does Lecture 10 contrast Lecture 9's better prompting with Lecture 10's better evidence for answering a film-club reading-pack question?
